topic: A person discovers the tree they planted as a child has been cut down
text: I remember the day we planted that tree, how small the sapling was then, barely reaching my knee. It always held a special place, a silent witness to the laughter and whispers of our backyard. The spot where it stood, now bare, feels different, almost hollow. I walk around it, my steps slower, softer, as if I’m afraid to disturb the memories that linger in the air. I can’t shake the thought of those young leaves, how they once reached for the sun, now gone. The garden is quiet now, too quiet, and the ground underfoot seems to echo that emptiness. I keep replaying the time we spent nurturing it, imagining the tree could somehow still be there, growing, just out of sight.
